france24fr.title: Qu'est-ce que la Patriot Platform, à l'origine des manifestations anti-migrants au Royaume-Uni ?

spiegel.title: Berlin: Stefan Evers (CDU) fordert Videoüberwachung zum Schutz Homosexueller
spiegel.description: Stefan Evers will mehr in die Sicherheit Homosexueller in Berlin investieren – und setzt dabei auf verstärkte Videoüberwachung. In Brasilien sei das erfolgreich gewesen, argumentiert der CDU-Kandidat.

spiegel.title: 9/11 im historischen Liveticker: Taliban-Regierung bietet den USA Gespräche über Auslieferung Osama bin Ladens an
spiegel.description: Rund 24 Stunden nach dem Terror in den USA verdichten sich Hinweise, das Al-Qaida-Führer Osama bin Laden der Drahtzieher ist. Die Feuerwehr in New York stellt auf Notbetrieb um. Dieser Liveblog rekonstruiert den Terroranschlag vom 11. September 2001.

spiegel.title: Bärbel Bas: Lars Klingbeil verteidigt SPD-Ministerin gegen CDU-Kritik
spiegel.description: Die heftige Attacke aus der Union gegen Arbeitsministerin Bärbel Bas sorgt für Empörung in der SPD: Bas’ Co-Parteichef Lars Klingbeil warnte die CDU vor einem Rechtskurs.

spiegel.title: Donald Trump in Irland: US-Präsident schwärmt von vereintem Irland
spiegel.description: Diese Aussage sorgt für Aufregung im Vereinigten Königreich: Bei einem Kurzbesuch in Dublin wünscht sich US-Präsident Donald Trump kurzerhand die Vereinigung Irlands mit Nordirland. Das fände er »fantastisch«.

spiegel.title: Tilda Swinton: Solo-Triumph mit »Jacke wie Hose« bzw. »Man to Man« eröffnet Londons Bühnensaison
spiegel.description: Ein Theaterstück aus Deutschland ist der Hit der frisch eröffneten Londoner Bühnensaison. Manfred Karges »Jacke wie Hose« heißt in der Version des Royal Court Theatre »Man to Man« – und ist ein Solo-Triumph für Tilda Swinton.

spiegel.title: Berlin Abgeordnetenhauswahl 2026: Diese Koalitionen sind möglich
spiegel.description: In Berlin zeichnet sich bei der Abgeordnetenhauswahl ein Kopf-an-Kopf-Rennen ab. Laut neuesten Umfragen sind vor allem zwei Koalitionen denkbar. Testen Sie mit unserem Rechner, wann welche Regierungsoption möglich wird.

spiegel.title: Giorgia Meloni über AfD: Brandmauer funktioniert nicht
spiegel.description: Die italienische Ministerpräsidentin Giorgia Meloni kritisiert Deutschlands Umgang mit der AfD. Gleichzeitig grenzt sie sich von den Rechtsextremen ab.

spiegel.title: Julia Beautx: Influencerin kündigt Auszeit an
spiegel.description: Julia Beautx will eine Schaffenspause auf unbestimmte Zeit einlegen. Die Influencerin kündigte diesen Schritt auf Instagram an. Sie müsse sich wieder klar werden, »wer ich sein will, was ich machen möchte«.

spiegel.title: Wirtschaftsreformen: Kretschmer drängt Merz zu Gesprächen mit Gewerkschaften
spiegel.description: Nach der Wahl in Sachsen-Anhalt steht Friedrich Merz unter Druck. Sachsens Ministerpräsident Michael Kretschmer fordert, Deutschland müsse wieder wettbewerbsfähiger werden. Dem Kanzler gibt er einen Tipp.

spiegel.title: Quiz des Tages beim SPIEGEL: 7 Fragen zum Allgemeinwissen pro Tag
spiegel.description: Jeden Tag gibt es sieben Fragen zu den wichtigsten Themengebieten des politisch-gesellschaftlichen Geschehens. Testen Sie hier Ihr Wissen!

spiegel.title: US Open: Alexander Zverevs langer Aufschlag irritiert Gegner Chatschanow
spiegel.description: US-Open-Finalist Alexander Zverev ist gefürchtet für seine kraftvollen Aufschläge. Doch etwas daran störte Halbfinalgegner Chatschanow: Der Deutsche lässt den Ball vorher sehr oft aufspringen.

spiegel.title: Streit über Termingarantie: Kassenärzte stellen schnellere Facharzttermine in Aussicht – bei medizinischer Notwendigkeit
spiegel.description: Eine Termingarantie beim Facharzt lehnen die Kassenärzte weiter ab. Für bestimmte Fälle allerdings könne es eine Lösung geben, sagt Verbandschef Gassen – mit »einer entsprechenden Vergütung«.

spiegel.title: Deutschland: Fast jeder zweite Schüler schläft laut DAK schlecht
spiegel.description: Deutschlands Jugend schläft zu wenig. Mehr als zwei Drittel der Befragten klagten bei einer Untersuchung der DAK außerdem über Erschöpfung. Laut der Krankenkasse könnte das zu den Pisa-Ergebnissen beigetragen haben.

spiegel.title: Großbritannien: Rekordspenden für britische Rechtspartei Reform UK
spiegel.description: Unheimlicher Geldsegen für Großbritanniens Rechtspopulisten: Nigel Farages Partei Reform UK hat zwei gigantische Einzelspenden erhalten. In beiden Fällen stecken Krypto-Unternehmer dahinter.

spiegel.title: Fantasy-Serie »City of Blood«: Die nächste Serien-Katastrophe aus Deutschland
spiegel.description: In »City of Blood« leiden die Berliner unter dem Klimawandel, und Vampire saugen die Stadt aus. Die Serie basiert auf einer großartigen Comic-Reihe, aber die Leute hinter dem Projekt wollen »Themen der Gegenwart«. Es ist zum Heulen.

spiegel.title: Fair Fashion: Wie nachhaltige Marken in der Krise um Kundschaft kämpfen
spiegel.description: Fair Fashion ist out. In der Krise halten Menschen ihr Geld lieber zusammen. Einige Marken wie Everlane sind bereits verkauft oder pleite – andere entwickeln kreative Ideen fürs Überleben.

spiegel.title: Cansin Köktürk: Linken-Abgeordnete muss wegen Zwischenrufen 2000 Euro zahlen
spiegel.description: Hitzige Szene im Bundestag: Die Linkenpolitikerin Cansin Köktürk reagiert aufgebracht auf eine Rede des AfD-Mannes René Springer. Nun wird es teuer für sie.

observador.title: Havana acusa Trump de "terrorismo de Estado"
observador.description: No 25.º aniversário do 11 de Setembro, Díaz-Canel denuncia embargo, bloqueio petrolífero e sanções como "plano genocida" contra o povo cubano.

observador.title: 70 empresas do calçado portuguesas em Milão
observador.description: BioShoes4All e FAIST são os projetos-bandeira nas feiras Lineapelle e Simac. Com quase 100 milhões investidos, o setor quer provar que Portugal é mais do que um fabricante de sapatos.

observador.title: Calor: 13 distritos sob aviso amarelo até segunda
observador.description: Évora, Lisboa, Setúbal e mais nove distritos vão estar sob aviso amarelo por temperaturas máximas elevadas. Norte do país junta-se a partir de domingo.

observador.title: 13h. Carlos Pereira concorda com relatório de Passos Coelho
observador.description: Ainda assim questiona as intenções do ex-primeiro-ministro e avisa que não podemos voltar ao passado. Ainda, Donald Trump repete que a guerra com o Irão vai acabar depois das eleições de novembro.

observador.title: Dragão testa invencibilidade, arbitragem volta a ser tema
observador.description: Sem Froholdt, o Porto procura manter o pleno em Rio Maior antes de receber o Benfica. Fora de campo, a PJ investiga pressões na arbitragem, enquanto o Estrela tenta a contratação de Renato Sanches.

observador.title: Caseiro detido pela PJ por suspeita de matar casal
observador.description: Homicídios terão ocorrido na habitação das duas vítimas. Suspeito terá arrastado os cadáveres para o interior de uma cisterna de água na propriedade e depois tentado decompô-los com químicos.

observador.title: Combustíveis. Carneiro acusa Chega de "enganar" portugueses
observador.description: Carneiro lembra que o Chega chumbou duas propostas socialistas de redução do IVA de 23% para 13% nos combustíveis antes de apoiar a terceira, na semana passada.

observador.title: Acordo UE-Mercosul resiste a Bolsonaro, diz FIBE
observador.description: Vitalino Canas defende que os "aspetos estruturais" do tratado superam os conjunturais. Portugal pode ser plataforma do Brasil no acordo, acrescenta.

observador.title: México enterra 117 corpos não identificados na Ciudad Juárez
observador.description: Autoridades forenses do estado mexicano de Chihuahua autorizaram o enterro de 117 corpos não identificados. Cada sepultura é registada e pode ser reaberta se chegar uma identificação.

observador.title: Homem acusado de abusos sexuais à enteada em Torres Vedras
observador.description: Padrasto começou a conviver com a vítima e os seus irmãos quando iniciou um relacionamento amoroso com a mãe deles há sete anos. Homem foi detido pela PJ após denúncia da mãe.

observador.title: 12h. Estruturas da PSP e GNR não abdicam das greves
observador.description: Ainda assim veem com bons olhos a convocatória. Ainda, três civis morreram e dezenas ficaram feridos em novos ataques da Rússia contra a Ucrânia.

observador.title: O estudo de Passos Coelho é uma arma de combate político?
observador.description: Carlos Pereira (PS) considera que o estudo de Passos Coelho serve para alimentar a disputa interna no PSD contra Montenegro. Já Sandra Ribeiro (CH) diz que pode ser uma "mais-valia" para o país.

observador.title: Ventura desafia PS. Carneiro evita alinhamento com Chega
observador.description: PS e Chega avançam com medidas idênticas sobre combustíveis e cabaz essencial, mas com instrumentos diferentes. Ventura desafia Carneiro a aprovar, mas PS teme risco para a imagem das contas certas.

observador.title: Organização sarauí denuncia atuação de Marrocos em Ceuta
observador.description: Em Lisboa, o presidente da AFAPREDESA acusou Marrocos de tortura, desaparecimentos forçados e bloqueio a visitas da ONU e Cruz Vermelha ao Saara Ocidental.

observador.title: Bolieiro convida diáspora açoriana a regressar
observador.description: O presidente do Governo Regional visitou a comunidade açoriana em Toronto e Brampton, onde inaugura uma réplica das Portas da Cidade de Ponta Delgada.

observador.title: Que fábrica é esta que produz o VW T-Roc e vai fechar?
observador.description: Há uma fábrica na Alemanha que produz o VW T-Roc, o mesmo modelo fabricado em Portugal, que vai ser encerrada. Que fábrica é esta e até que ponto pode a decisão alastrar à “nossa” Autoeuropa?

observador.title: Incêndios: GNR alerta para perigo nos próximos dias
observador.description: Temperaturas acima de 35ºC nos próximos dias preocupam a GNR, que recorda que mais de metade dos incêndios rurais tem origem em negligência humana.

observador.title: A falta de professores provoca ainda mais desigualdades?
observador.description: Com milhares de alunos a iniciar o ano sem aulas a várias disciplinas, cresce a corrida ao privado, o que aprofunda a desigualdade na educação. Ainda, a queda no PISA reflete anos de falhas políticas.

republika.title: Hamilton contro il muro a Madrid nelle terze libere. Comanda Antonelli davanti a Leclerc
republika.description: Errore all’ultima curva del tracciato per il britannico, Kimi velocissimo, ma la Ferrari c’è. Alle 16 le qualifiche per la pole

republika.title: Trump in visita a Dublino: “L’Irlanda tornerà a essere unita: sarà bellissimo”
republika.description: Le dichiarazioni del presidente americano (“prima o poi succederà”) scatenano polemiche e riaccendono il dibattito su un referendum per la riunificazione, come chiede Sinn Féin. Furia dei protestanti: “Così si distrugge il Regno Unito”

republika.title: Bezzecchi, giro record e pole a Misano: “La moto funziona”. In prima fila Marc Marquez e Aldeguer
republika.description: Il pilota dell’Aprilia davanti a tutti, alle sue spalle lo spagnolo. Solo 14° Bagnaia

republika.title: Treno deragliato in Francia, la polizia indaga per sabotaggio
republika.description: L’ipotesi degli inquirenti è che si sia trattato di un atto premeditato. L’incidente, avvenuto ieri sera nel nord del Paese nei pressi di Cléon, ha causato 44 feriti, di cui una donna ricoverata in gravi condizioni

republika.title: Il dribbling di Teheran alle sanzioni: soldi all’Iran dalle banche Usa
republika.description:
Le restrizioni di Trump non riescono a fermare
il flusso di dollari che attraverso le triangolazioni internazionali finiscono nel paese in guerra

republika.title: Dalle Bestie di Satana ai suprematisti, due milioni di italiani nella rete dei santoni. “Così manipolano le menti”
republika.description: Sono due milioni gli italiani che finiscono in una setta. Nel suo nuovo libro il giornalista Stefano Nazzi racconta le storie più inquietanti

republika.title: Guru e santoni, il reato di plagio non esiste più. E la legge antisette non c’è ancora
republika.description: E le persone fragili sono sempre a rischio. Mentre il Senato discute...

republika.title: Pierfrancesco Favino, frate in “Dio ride”: “Oggi sono meno rigido, mi diverto di più”
republika.description: L’attore chiude Venezia con il film di Giovanni Veronesi: “Mi piacerebbe avere il coraggio di non fare compromessi”. E racconta la sua idea di cinema, la forza della risata e il nuovo incontro con Bellocchio

republika.title: Di Battista arrivato a Roma e ricoverato al Gemelli. Il rientro da Cuba dopo l’intervento d’urgenza
republika.description: L’ex parlamentare è partito ieri dall’Avana a bordo di un’aeroambulanza. Il viaggio di circa 12 ore organizzato a tappe e a bassa quota

republika.title: Una lumaca fermerà Trump? Un’altra sala da ballo, nel suo golf club in Irlanda, fa discutere
republika.description: Il presidente Usa arriva oggi in visita sull’isola, tra grandi proteste previste. E un architetto, in nome di un mollusco raro, sta facendo la guerra al suo progetto di “Ballroom”, nel lussuoso resort di “The Donald” in un minuscolo villaggio sull’Oceano Atlantico

republika.title: Legge elettorale: preferenze e donne, Meloni teme agguati nella roulette Camera
republika.description: La premier: “L’Afd? No a parallelismi con l’Italia”. I sospetti su FI dopo le parole di Craxi in aula. La Russa giovedì al Colle

republika.title: Legge elettorale, il nodo firme. Le opposizioni: “Nuova porcata”
republika.description: Approvata la norma del centrodestra che prevede per le liste non presenti in Parlamento seimila sottoscrizioni per collegio. Conte chiede l’intervento del Colle. L’aiuto per Onorato

republika.title: L’abbraccio Franceschini-Renzi: “Le primarie non siano dilanianti”
republika.description: I due insieme alla festa dell’Unità. Il fondatore di Iv: “Salis o Manfredi al tavolo del programma per l’area moderata”

republika.title: Pd, mossa di Schlein sulla segreteria: proroga fino al voto
republika.description: Il mandato in scadenza a marzo, idea assemblea a ottobre per modificare lo statuto. Ma tra i dem spunta l’ipotesi congresso

republika.title: Marcello Crivellini, l’ex compagno di Bonino: “I viaggi, le prime battaglie e la polizia alla porta”
republika.description: I due non hanno mai interrotto il legame iniziato negli anni Settanta: “Ci siamo conosciuti in una scuola. Era sempre a casa mia quando era ricercata”

republika.title: Bonino, il muro della sinistra che non capì l’uso del corpo e il rapporto con Berlusconi
republika.description: L’antica distanza che contrapponeva le culture politiche si è nel tempo attenuata. Il Pci garantì la massa critica per rendere legge le battaglie su divorzio e aborto

republika.title: Emma Bonino, al Cairo scoprì che la democrazia non si può esportare
republika.description:
Dopo le politiche del 2001 andò in Egitto in cerca di nuove battaglie.
All’inizio era favorevole alla guerra in Iraq, ma poi ammise l’errore

republika.title: Castellina ricorda Bonino: “Quante liti ma ci abbracciammo per il voto sul divorzio”
republika.description: La storica comunista: “In cinquant’anni siamo sempre state separate. Non era di sinistra, difendeva i diritti individuali, non i collettivi”

nyt.title: How Trump Is Wielding Power to Stifle Speech
nyt.description: President Trump has harnessed agencies across the government to curtail press freedoms, a sweeping campaign that free speech advocates say will have lasting effects.

nyt.title: In Doonbeg, Trump’s Irish Open Visit Prompts Protests and Praise
nyt.description: As the U.S. president heads to his Doonbeg hotel for the Irish Open, locals expressed both appreciation for the resort’s economic benefits and opposition to his politics.

nyt.title: Visa Issue Threatens U.S.-Brazil Cooperation on Crime
nyt.description: Officials say the Trump administration is blocking some of Brazil’s efforts to expand cooperation on fighting transnational crime.

nyt.title: Inflation Complicates Trump’s Midterms Pitch to Voters
nyt.description: Gas prices are high, mortgage rates are climbing and inflation remains well above target, complicating the president’s midterm appeal.

nyt.title: Republicans, Facing Midterm Peril, Try to Brand Democrats as Communists
nyt.description: Communism, in the president’s hyperbolic telling, is a graver threat to the country than the Pearl Harbor or 9/11 attacks were. Whether this midterm strategy works is an open question.

nyt.title: Trump Wanted a New House Map in Missouri. Voters Got Chaos Instead.
nyt.description: The legal wrangling over a congressional map redrawn by Republicans has election officials, candidates and voters scrambling before November.

nyt.title: Saudi Oil Exports Face Heightened Threats After Attacks on Pipeline
nyt.description: Ship operators already faced severe risks in navigating the region, and now the danger is higher as Houthi militias assert control in the Red Sea.

nyt.title: ‘We Left in the Clothes We Were Wearing’: Yemenis Flee New Fighting
nyt.description: Hunger and disease have tormented Yemen for years. Now, fighting between the Saudi-backed government and Iran-backed Houthis is pushing it to the brink.

nyt.title: Why Mokha, Historic Port That Shaped the Coffee Trade, Is a Prize in Yemen’s War
nyt.description: A strategic location on the Red Sea afforded the city centuries of trading dominance — and makes it a coveted target in today’s fighting in the Middle East.

nyt.title: Inside the Discussions at AI Companies Over a Superintelligence Doomsday
nyt.description: Researchers at Anthropic, OpenAI, Meta and Google are increasingly trying to raise awareness about the risks of artificial intelligence.

nyt.title: Why It’s Difficult for Tech Companies to Rein In A.I.
nyt.description: Researchers say artificial intelligence is developing faster than the systems put in place to monitor and control it.

nyt.title: Naomi Klein and Astra Taylor Say the End of the World Is Now on the Table
nyt.description: In a new book, the writers argue that a powerful coalition of “end times fascists” is just fine with the earth’s demise.

nyt.title: Why Tech Oligarchs Are Willing to Risk Apocalypse
His Act Is Getting Old
nyt.description: The $5,000 election promise shows how afraid Trump really is.

nyt.title: Walk This Way
nyt.description: Are there everyday activities that you can turn into a walk?

nyt.title: New York Marks the 25th Anniversary of 9/11 at Ground Zero
nyt.description: At a ceremony in Lower Manhattan, elected officials and loved ones of those killed in the 2001 terror attacks gathered in solemn remembrance.

npr.title: 'BRICS' forum brings together emerging economies, aimed at countering western dominance
npr.description: India hosts the 18th BRICS summit in New Delhi this weekend. BRICS is a grouping of major emerging markets and developing countries.

npr.title: Saudi Arabia forced to shut down crucial Red Sea pipeline after attacks
npr.description: The Iran-backed Houthi militia captured a strategic Red Sea port city this week. NPR's Scott Simon talks to April Longley Alley of the Washington Institute.

npr.title: The secret quest to preserve Palestinian writer Raja Shehadeh's diaries
npr.description: Leading Palestinian writer Raja Shehadeh has documented Israel's occupation of the West Bank since day one. Fearing the occupation might consume his archive, he secretly moved it to Scotland

npr.title: BRICS leaders meet in India as wars and US tensions test the bloc
npr.description: Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi hosts Russian President Vladimir Putin, Chinese President Xi Jinping and other leaders of the BRICS nations for a summit on trade, investment, and global conflicts.

npr.title: Yemen's Houthis capture a Red Sea island in threat to shipping
npr.description: Iranian-backed Houthi rebels in Yemen have captured a strategic island in the Bab el-Mandeb Strait. The move threatens Saudi oil exports through a key commercial lane. And Saudi Arabia said it shut down a major oil pipeline as a precaution after it came under attack.

npr.title: The other side of 9/11: Afghans reckon with America's long shadow
npr.description: It's been nearly 25 years since the start of the U.S- led invasion of Afghanistan. NPR returns to Kabul to see how Afghans, now back under Taliban rule, are coping with the legacy of that 20 year war.

npr.title: Amid war and sanctions, many Iranians are losing their jobs and struggling to get by
npr.description: Many Iranians lost their jobs because of the war and the U.S. blockade. Now some are even losing their backup jobs as sanctions tighten.

npr.title: The U.S.-Canada trade war is creating a headache for auto-parts makers
npr.description: For decades, the U.S. and Canadian auto supply chains have been tightly woven together. The trade war is threatening to unravel a complex system.

npr.title: Why gains by Iran-backed Houthis in Yemen could push gas prices even higher
npr.description: A Houthi advance along Yemen's Red Sea coast could help push gas prices up even more as the Iran-backed group also launches attacks on Saudi Arabia's oil facilities.

npr.title: Hong Kong court sentences 3 Tiananmen vigil organizers to prison
npr.description: The activists were sentenced to about 5 to 7 years in prison in a case widely seen as a barometer of the city's eroding freedoms as Beijing clamps down on dissent.

elpais.title: Los riesgos de la IA según los que la han visto desde dentro: “El mundo no está preparado y nosotros no estamos preparados”
elpais.description: Una decena de investigadores, directivos y expertos que abandonaron OpenAI, Google o Anthropic han alertado en los últimos años de fallos de seguridad, usos militares y sistemas cada vez más difíciles de controlar por estas compañías. Estos son sus temores

elpais.title: La guerra abierta en la Delegación de Ceuta por los avisos del salto fronterizo atrapa al Gobierno en un nuevo cruce de versiones
elpais.description: La dimisión del jefe de gabinete del delegado tras afirmar que sí informó del aviso del CNI abre otro frente al Ejecutivo seis semanas después del inicio de la crisis

elpais.title: ¿A quién beneficia la crisis de Ceuta?
elpais.description: En el balance salen arriba en la lista aquellos que quieren el fracaso del proyecto europeo

elpais.title: De Indra a Correos y la ‘ley de nietos’: cuatro años del PP y Vox renovando la teoría de la trampa electoral
elpais.description: Los partidos de Feijóo y Abascal han convertido en recurrente la acusación al Gobierno de intentar torcer el voto a su favor

elpais.title: Irene Montero anuncia que se someterá a primarias abiertas para liderar la izquierda en las generales y obliga a Sumar a posicionarse
elpais.description: La exministra llama a cambiar las reglas del sistema: “Vida solo hay una y planeta solo hay uno, así que la política se tiene que dedicar a lo básico”

elpais.title: El último presidente de la Segunda República
elpais.description: José Maldonado vivió melancólicamente al cobijo de los intelectuales extranjeros mientras en España fue condenado al olvido

elpais.title: Peter Sloterdijk, filósofo: “La gente que deposita su ira en la AfD perderá dinero, perderá la esperanza y perderá las ilusiones”
elpais.description: El pensador alemán ve paralelismos entre Alternativa para Alemania y el partido nazi y alerta de que la IA genera sensación de inutilidad: urge que recuperemos el sentido de nuestras vidas

elpais.title: Zoe Bonafonte: “Hay que disfrutar cada proyecto como si fuera el último y gestionar bien  el dinero, por favor”
elpais.description: La descubrimos hace dos años en ‘El 47’. Ahora la actriz se confirma como uno de los referentes jóvenes de talento y confianza

elpais.title: Comprar y alquilar casa en 24 horas por miedo a perderla: estos son los riesgos de las operaciones exprés
elpais.description: La escasez de oferta y la presión de la demanda empujan a muchos compradores e inquilinos a tomar decisiones en minutos sin verificar el estado físico y legal de la casa

elpais.title: “Busco mujer para sexo después de misa”: cuando encontrábamos pareja a través de los anuncios por palabras
elpais.description: Antes de que los chats de Internet los dejasen anticuados y las aplicaciones de ligue tomasen el control de nuestra existencia, los anuncios por palabras en la prensa eran la única manera de buscar pareja desde casa

elpais.title: La obscenidad sin límites del rey del mundo
elpais.description: Todo en la gestualidad de Donald Trump, en su voz, en su presencia física, incita a la grima

elpais.title: Ruiz Zafón y el mundillo literario
elpais.description: No conocí ese mundillo hasta casi los 40 años. Al cabo de dos o tres cócteles, ya me había empachado

elpais.title: Querida niña Gala
elpais.description: A veces he sentido que eres una especie de cariátide en miniatura que sostiene, con su alegría, los frisos del mundo

elpais.title: El saber ya no ocupa lugar
elpais.description: En España el progreso de la ignorancia está apostillado por la pontificación de los expertos y de los políticos

elpais.title: Qué es la inteligencia y por qué va a acabar con nosotros
elpais.description: Me pregunto dónde está la tecnología capaz de decirnos si estamos construyendo un mundo amable y si nos gusta donde y cómo vivimos. Ni está ni se la espera

elpais.title: ¿Han empeorado todos los estudiantes por igual? Nueve gráficos sobre los datos de PISA
elpais.description: La caída es general, pero no todos han bajado igual: pierden más los alumnos con más recursos, los de centros privados, los extranjeros y comunidades como la Valenciana. Quienes más tiempo pasan en las redes sociales sacan peores notas

elpais.title: Las chicas van un curso por delante en lectura y los chicos llevan medio año de ventaja en matemáticas
elpais.description: Las alumnas acaban con la histórica brecha en los resultados de ciencias, según el Informe PISA

elpais.title: El ultra Farage recibe 42 millones de un empresario cripto, la mayor donación individual de la historia del Reino Unido
elpais.description: El regalo del polémico empresario Ben Delo resucita el debate sobre los límites legales de estas ayudas

phys-org.title: Why are the stars around our galaxy's black hole missing their companions?
phys-org.description: A new study suggests that the young stars orbiting the Milky Way's central black hole may have a surprisingly ordinary origin. But the black hole's influence may be what makes their origin look more exotic than it really is. Along with shaping their orbits, it may also destroy their stellar companions. The paper outlining this work was published in Astronomy & Astrophysics on Aug. 11.

phys-org.title: Rubin observatory peers deep into the famous COSMOS field
phys-org.description: The COSMOS field, or Cosmic Evolution Survey Deep Field, is one of the most famous patches of the universe observed by astronomers. Located in the constellation Sextans, this region was photographed by the Hubble Space Telescope (HST) in segments from 2003 to 2005 using its Advanced Camera for Surveys (ACS). With support from ground-based and other space-based telescopes, the resulting images were then stitched together to create a stunning picture of cosmic evolution.

phys-org.title: As antibiotic resistance grows, researchers turn to copper to fight infections
phys-org.description: When bacteria invade the urinary tract, the body has its own arsenal for fighting back. Among those weapons is an unlikely tool: copper. Researchers at the Texas A&M College of Veterinary Medicine and Biomedical Sciences (VMBS) are investigating how the body uses the essential trace mineral to fight urinary tract infections (UTIs), how bacteria manage to survive that attack and whether those discoveries could eventually lead to new ways of treating infections that are increasingly difficult to c

phys-org.title: Nepal flood disaster exposes cascading threats in Himalayas
phys-org.description: A catastrophic flood in Nepal that left thousands missing began with a collapse of ice and rock high in the mountains—a warning that disaster planning must prepare for chains of hazards, not isolated events, experts say.

phys-org.title: Q&A: The origin of 'OnlyMarms' and what made it a roaring success
phys-org.description: The story of Dan Blumstein's decision to share videos of marmots from the Rocky Mountain Biological Laboratory field study on an OnlyFans account called OnlyMarms has captured attention around the world over the past few weeks.

phys-org.title: Bridging interfacial water structure and reactivity in photocatalytic hydrogen evolution at TiO₂ interfaces
phys-org.description: Hydrogen (H2) evolution via photocatalytic water splitting is an environmentally friendly and sustainable technology for solar-to-chemical energy conversion. Although interfacial interactions are recognized as key determinants of photocatalytic performance, systematic experimental studies explicitly targeting the structure and reactivity of the water-catalyst interface remain limited. A major challenge lies in probing the molecular structure of interfacial water, especially under hydrogen-evolvi

phys-org.title: How one RNA nucleotide switch activates fluorescent dyes
phys-org.description: RhoBAST is a tiny RNA molecule that activates fluorescent dyes, enabling researchers to track RNA molecules in living cells with super-resolution. An international collaboration, which includes Ronald Micura and his team from the Institute of Organic Chemistry, has now shown that a small, local "nucleotide flip" within the RNA controls this fluorescence activation.

phys-org.title: How big can the universe's first starbursts get?
phys-org.description: As our telescopes have improved and we've been able to peer farther back in time, we've begun finding more fascinating features of the universe. But one thing we haven't found for sure is Population III (Pop III) stars. These were the earliest stars in the universe, formed completely from pristine hydrogen and helium, with no "metals" (i.e., elements heavier than those two) polluting their processes.

phys-org.title: Smart, self-healing packaging uses AI to detect food spoilage in real time
phys-org.description: Packaging already tells us where food comes from, when it was made, what's in it and how many calories it contains. But researchers see a future where packaging can "see," in real time, what's happening inside and translate that into information that producers and consumers can act on.

phys-org.title: Single nanostructure enables independent control of two light resonance modes
phys-org.description: Metallic nanostructures are exceptionally effective at concentrating light into tiny volumes, while dielectric nanostructures excel at storing light with minimal energy loss. Combining these complementary properties has traditionally required complicated hybrid structures in which the two optical modes become mixed, making them difficult to control independently.

phys-org.title: New genome study rewrites the early history of grasses, the world's most important plant family
phys-org.description: An international team of scientists, including Donald Danforth Plant Science Center member emerita Elizabeth "Toby" Kellogg, Ph.D., has produced a chromosome-level genome assembly that offers a new view of the earliest evolution of grasses, the plant family that includes many of the world's most important food crops.

phys-org.title: AI helps find hidden human proteins and reveals what they do
phys-org.description: New research shows how artificial intelligence, combined with advanced experimental science, can help find "hidden" and unexplored proteins in the human body and reveal what they actually do, according to a new study published in Nature.

phys-org.title: Emerging SARS-CoV-2 sublineage RE.2.2 displays distinct structural features
phys-org.description: Researchers from the Institute of Microbiology of the Chinese Academy of Sciences (IMCAS) have characterized the structural and functional properties of the emerging SARS-CoV-2 sublineage BA.3.2.2 by studying RE.2.2, the lineage designation for the BA.3.2.2 branch gaining prevalence after prolonged low detection in European surveillance datasets.

phys-org.title: Compost microbe yields enzyme that tackles polyurethane foam and nylon
phys-org.description: Researchers from Aarhus University and the Danish Technological Institute have taken a new approach in the search for enzymes capable of breaking down some of the most difficult types of plastic to recycle. They collected millions of bacteria from a landfill in Kenya, Randers Regnskov Tropical Zoo, the guts of larvae and a compost heap near Aarhus—and examined their enzymes. They found 12 that work.

phys-org.title: Microplastics fall across rural Switzerland, adding over 200 tons yearly to land and water
phys-org.description: Loose fibers from functional clothing, discarded PET bottles or abandoned packaging: When such plastic materials enter the environment, they often persist there for a long time. UV radiation, precipitation and ozone cause them to become brittle—and over time, mechanical forces break them down into increasingly smaller particles. Swirled up by the wind, they are carried farther through the atmosphere. Until now, it was unclear how much microplastic ends up back in Swiss soil and water bodies thro

phys-org.title: 10,000 years of wheat and barley selection reveal shared climate-adaptation genes
phys-org.description: Research teams from INRAE, the University of Clermont Auvergne and the CNRS have reconstructed 10 ancient genomes (paleogenomes) that are the common ancestors of 84 botanical species of agronomic interest. Their work makes it possible to identify particular genes, shared across different species of plants and retained throughout their evolutionary history, that might play a key role in adapting to environmental constraints such as drought.

phys-org.title: New measure captures how scientists' identities shift across academic disciplines
phys-org.description: Does the academic discipline of a scientist's doctorate accurately capture their disciplinary affiliation decades later? Consider a scientist who earned a doctorate in physics 25 years ago who now studies climate change, publishes primarily in interdisciplinary journals and considers herself a climate scientist. Does "physics" still accurately describe where she fits in science?

phys-org.title: When will your glacier disappear? New website lets users explore risks worldwide
phys-org.description: When will the glacier in your valley disappear? Will the glacier you visited as a child still exist in 2050? And how much difference would limiting global warming make?

undark.title: Review: A Vision of a Future Where Machines Fight Wars
undark.description: In “Lethal Autonomy,” Frank Kendall, a former top defense department official, envisions a military future where vehicles and weapons operate largely on their own — including making some decisions to strike people or infrastructure. And in his view, conflict is coming to space, making it all more urgent.

undark.title: Book Review: The Messy Business of Making Science Happen
undark.description: In “Lost in Curiosity: Field Notes From Scientists’ Adventures Into the Unknown,” Roberta Kwok sets out to smash the stereotype of eureka moments as the main drivers of scientific knowledge, largely by taking us inside the everyday world of science and scientists, in all its painstaking monotony.

undark.title: Book Review: Our Conflicted Relationship with the Sun
undark.description: Despite dermatological guidelines that decree sunlight a harmful carcinogen, Rowan Jacobsen argues in “In Defense of Sunlight” that the sun helps our skin produce many compounds vital to our health. How did science miss these benefits? The answer, he says, lies in our inability to do things in moderation.

undark.title: The New Student Visa Policy Doesn’t Add Up
undark.description: In July, the Department of Homeland Security issued new rules that would make it harder for international students to complete their studies in the U.S. The policy threatens to be disruptive for students — particularly doctoral candidates — and self-defeating for the country.

undark.title: Book Review: How Wildlife Is Returning to the East
undark.description: In “The Beasts of the East,” journalist Andrew Moore charts the natural history of the East and the people who have dedicated their careers to restoring several long lost species to what remains of their original habitats.

undark.title: Book Review: The Case for the AI-Powered Global Brain
undark.description: In “The God Test,” Robert Wright considers a future in which human consciousness becomes infused with AI. “We have to think seriously about a future in which there is something that increasingly resembles a global brain, and its neurons increasingly consist not just of human brains but of AIs,” he writes.

undark.title: Interview: How Tragedy Changed the FDA
undark.description: As an FDA advisory committee prepares to weigh whether specialized pharmacies should be allowed to dispense seven unapproved peptides, Mikkael A. Sekeres, a scientist and former adviser, discusses the history and nuances of FDA oversight, including its process for screening advisory committee members for conflicts of interest.

undark.title: Will AI Fix Prior Authorization — or Make It Worse?
undark.description: The Trump administration is currently piloting a program in six states that expands Medicare prior authorizations using AI tools in an effort to reduce unnecessary medical spending. But it remains to be seen whether this new approach, which the administration has called “broken” in the private sector, will be effective without causing dangerous delays for Medicare recipients.

undark.title: Biologists Should Articulate Their Position on AI
undark.description: Last month, mathematics researchers released the Leiden Declaration, a treatise on how to handle the challenges that artificial intelligence poses to their field. C. Brandon Ogbunu argues that biologists should learn from the mathematics community and work on their own version.

undark.title: Review: What Animals Can Teach Humans About Caregiving
undark.description: From seahorses and birds to beetles and killer whales, journalist Elizabeth Preston finds a lot of common ground  between human and animal parenting in “The Creatures’ Guide to Caring,” a sweeping survey of the evolution of caregiving and the dizzying array of survival strategies in the animal kingdom.

proj-syn.title: AI Could Make Governments Slower
proj-syn.description: Governments are increasingly turning to AI tools to process vast amounts of information and make public services more efficient. But because human attention is finite, making machines more capable could simply create new bottlenecks wherever oversight is necessary.

proj-syn.title: Why Do So Few Women Work in India?
proj-syn.description: India’s female labor force participation rate has long lagged behind that of peer economies like Bangladesh, not because of social norms, but because of weak demand for labor. That is ultimately good news, because it is a problem that can be solved with common-sense regulatory reforms and public investment.

proj-syn.title: Global Development’s Missing Ingredient
proj-syn.description: Facing a democracy deficit worldwide, millions of vulnerable people lack avenues through which they can collectively negotiate their interests. Faith-based institutions committed to human dignity and pluralism can play an instrumental role in building the infrastructure required for grassroots organizing at scale.

proj-syn.title: China’s External Surplus Makes a “Mandarin Accord” Inevitable
proj-syn.description: As with the Plaza Accord in 1985, when the United States and its major trading partners agreed to coordinate policies to weaken the US dollar, an agreement to address global imbalances emanating from China has become increasingly necessary. Given China’s undervalued currency, the situation simply cannot be sustained indefinitely.

proj-syn.title: War and Climate
proj-syn.description: The closure of the Strait of Hormuz showed how quickly a regional conflict can throw global energy markets into chaos. By pushing governments toward coal and biofuels, the war could accelerate deforestation and undermine climate negotiations, with environmental consequences that will linger long after the fighting ends.

proj-syn.title: 9/11’s Long Shadow
proj-syn.description: As tragic as the terrorist attacks of September 11, 2001, were, it was America’s response that truly changed the world. While it is difficult to pinpoint precisely which developments over the last 25 years were caused or compounded by 9/11, it seems clear that the event led the United States to abandon the principles that, with the Cold War over, were supposed to shape a better future.

proj-syn.title: The False Politics of Western Declinism
proj-syn.description: Political leaders on both sides of the Atlantic increasingly portray the West as being in decline, even as their societies grow richer. By conflating a loss of relative economic power with falling living standards, they give populists an opening to turn domestic grievances into nationalist resentment.

proj-syn.title: What 9/11 Did to Us
proj-syn.description: For Americans who are old enough to remember them, the September 11, 2001, terrorist attacks raised fundamental questions: Who could have done this, and above all, why? We now know that the answers would reshape the country and its place in the world—and not for the better.

proj-syn.title: After the AI Bubble Bursts
proj-syn.description: Just as debt markets fueled the global financial near-meltdown that followed the 2007–08 subprime-mortgage crisis, their exposure to AI will drive developments now. The problem is that we possess only very limited public information about those markets, and regulators are not making that information any easier to obtain.

proj-syn.title: Trump Is Stoking Territorial Revisionism
proj-syn.description: Donald Trump’s refusal to respect international borders has already led Argentina and Morocco to revive territorial disputes and has effectively given Israel carte blanche to operate where it sees fit. But this might be just the beginning: if the US can claim land and resources on the basis of vague national-security claims, anyone can.

proj-syn.title: Have the Terrorists Won?
proj-syn.description: The point of terrorism is not to cause suffering, but to provoke the target into doing something that hurts it even more. In the quarter-century since the 9/11 attacks, the US has done just that, leaving the world and itself worse off.

proj-syn.title: How 9/11 Fractured the Global Order
proj-syn.description: The terrorist attack on the United States 25 years ago remains among the most consequential events of this century. By fundamentally altering the trajectories of the United States and Russia, as well as that of a rising China, al-Qaeda’s attack set in motion developments that would produce the geopolitical tumult we live in today.

proj-syn.title: China’s Permanent Manufacturing Revolution
proj-syn.description: In developed economies, manufacturing employment will decline, regardless of industrial strategies pursued. China's competitiveness means that any expectation that manufacturing will absorb more than a trivial fraction of the large increases in the working-age population still occurring in India or Africa is a delusion.

proj-syn.title: Europe Needs Dual-Use Defense Spending
proj-syn.description: Some EU countries, such as Poland, are using their expanded defense budgets to buy more foreign hardware. A better approach would be to foster a thriving innovation ecosystem which ensures that the technologies, institutions, and people that underpin a strong military benefit the civilian economy as well.

proj-syn.title: The World 9/11 Didn’t Make
proj-syn.description: Looking back at the past quarter-century, it becomes apparent that the 9/11 terrorist attack against the United States was not a transformative event. Far more important developments have intervened, not least America’s rejection of the postwar order that it had a large hand in building.

proj-syn.title: The BRICS at 20
proj-syn.description: If the promise of the BRICS was to establish a monetary union, a single market, or a tightly integrated political alliance, it has not been fulfilled. But if it was to build a platform for emerging economies to cooperate while advancing their own strategic autonomy, the BRICS has exceeded expectations.

proj-syn.title: Europe’s Security Depends on a Clear Electrification Target
proj-syn.description: The politics around electrification are beginning to shift in Europe as more people recognize its importance for economic competitiveness and industrial resilience. European Union policymakers should seize this momentum to embed a binding target of at least 50% electrification by 2040 in the bloc’s energy security framework.
